words.definition: feeling pleasure or joy
words.example: I am happy when I see my friends.

words.definition: feeling unhappy
words.example: She felt sad when her friend left.

words.definition: feeling strong dislike about something that is wrong or unfair
words.example: He was angry about the broken window.

words.definition: needing rest or sleep
words.example: I feel tired after work.

words.definition: feeling afraid of something
words.example: The little boy was scared of the dark.

words.definition: feeling very happy and full of energy about something
words.example: The children were excited about the trip.

words.definition: feeling unhappy because you think something bad may happen
words.example: My mother was worried about the storm.

words.definition: feeling shock because something happened that you did not expect
words.example: I was surprised to see my old friend.

words.definition: feeling tired and unhappy because something is not interesting
words.example: The students felt bored during the long class.

words.definition: feeling worried or afraid about something that will happen
words.example: I was nervous before my exam.

words.definition: not worried, angry, or excited
words.example: Please stay calm and listen carefully.

words.definition: feeling pleased about something good that you or someone else did
words.example: My parents are proud of my grades.

words.definition: feeling nervous about meeting or talking to other people
words.example: The new student is very shy.

words.definition: feeling sad because you are alone
words.example: He felt lonely in the new city.

words.definition: to have a certain emotion
words.example: I feel happy today.

words.definition: to make a sound that shows you are happy or think something is funny
words.example: We laughed at the funny movie.

words.definition: to have tears fall from your eyes, often because you are sad
words.example: The baby started to cry.

words.definition: to move your mouth to show that you are happy
words.example: She smiled when she saw the gift.

words.definition: to like someone or something very much
words.example: I love my family.

words.definition: to dislike someone or something very much
words.example: He hates waiting in long lines.

text: Everyone feels different emotions every day. This morning, I felt happy because the sun was shining. But then I remembered my exam, and I became a little nervous and worried. At school, my friend looked sad, so I asked her what was wrong. She said she felt lonely because her best friend moved to another city. I tried to make her smile, and soon she started to laugh with me. During the exam, some students felt scared, but I stayed calm and did my best. After the exam, I was excited to go home, and my teacher said she was proud of our class. On the bus, a loud noise made me feel surprised, and for a moment I was a little scared. My little brother was bored at home, so he watched a funny video and began to cry from laughing so hard! Sometimes we feel angry too, but it is important to talk about our feelings. I love my family and friends because they help me feel better on hard days.
